notes: 2024-11-05: Initial inbound demo request from platform infra team (CTO intro). Wants a 'drop-in' inference plane to replace internal serving stack.

2024-11-12: Discovery call (Maya + Diego) — workload: high-concurrency chat + personalization; 70% reads short (<64 tokens), 30% long context (<=8k).  Target: sub-200ms median for chat, p95 < 300ms, p99 < 500ms for SLOs.
2024-11-19: POC kickoff (Fireflies ff_2024-11-19_8472). POC scope: 2-week benchmark running Llama2-70B-compat quantized, evaluate batching, KV cache effectiveness, and sustained throughput.

Benchmark ask: provide sustained min tokens/sec guarantee across the Dedicated pool. Customer proposal: 35k tokens/sec sustained, 300 concurrent sessions baseline, 600 concurrent burst for up to 10 minutes per hour.

Redwood draft: commit to min 32k tokens/sec sustained (across reserved GPUs) with max sustained concurrency 300 and burst allowance 2x baseline for 15 minutes/hr, subject to fair-share and pre-warm cache. Customer pushing for explicit SLA credit if throughput dips below threshold for >5 consecutive minutes.

Reserved GPU planning: Horizon Bridge requests H100-equivalent reservation for peak month. Their estimate: 12 H100-eq nodes to meet 35k tokens/sec (based on their internal perf numbers). Ask: provide mapping table (tokens/sec per GPU at target mix) + warmup plan for KV cache to avoid initial cold-start TPS drops.

Latency / SLO negotiation points: they want p50 < 80ms for short chats, p95 < 200ms, p99 < 400ms on 2k context; Redwood recommended p99 budget up to 500ms on long 8k contexts and fallback to smaller model variant for hard SLOs. Discussed automatic fallback routing in case of capacity pressure.

Burst policy details under discussion: Horizon proposes guaranteed burst envelope (600 conc) for 10 min/hour and ability to buy extra burst credits. Redwood proposed soft-burst (best-effort) plus paid burst slots with pre-warmed capacity for firm bursts. Procurement prefers firm burst reservations with pricing tiers.

SLA language items: uptime SLA 99.95% for Dedicated control plane, throughput SLA defined as 'min sustained tokens/sec across reserved fleet' with penalty tiers at 10% and 25% shortfall. Legal seeks cap on cumulative credits. Redwood legal asked for examples of acceptable penalty caps — back-and-forth ongoing.

Security / compliance: filled initial security questionnaire (doc link). Customer requires SSO/SAML + KMS integration, audit log retention 2 years, and option for EU-only residency for PII. Private deployment option evaluated for regulated EU customers.

2024-11-27: On-site workshop with infra and SREs (ff_2024-11-27_9091). Focus: traffic shaping, concurrency limits per model, prefetching/prefix cache strategies. Action: Redwood to provide detailed perf matrix per instance type and quantization profile by 2024-12-05.

2024-12-03: POC results summary received — sustained tokens/sec ~33k on default quant; reach 36k with per-request batching + prefix caching. Customer requested a binding multiplier table mapping 'reserved GPUs -> guaranteed tokens/sec' for contract.

2024-12-10: Pricing/commit call with procurement. Horizon wants a 12-month reserved contract with quarterly true-ups. Key ask: explicit lead time for extra GPU capacity (they budget seasonal spikes). Redwood to add clause for 'burst pool' purchase with 2-week provisioning SLA.

Open technical asks: provide per-model concurrency ceiling guidance (e.g., L70B quant: 25 concurrent streams per H100-eq node at target latency) and recommended batching window to meet throughput without violating latency SLOs.

Next concrete deliverables: Redwood to send redlined SLA + throughput appendix (table of reserved GPU counts -> min tokens/sec -> concurrency caps -> burst allowances) by 2024-12-15. Horizon legal to review and return redlines by 2024-12-22.
